newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus police investigate deadly dog-fights.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus police investigate deadly dog-fights.

text.p: Police in Cyprus said on Thursday they were investigating deadly dog fights held for betting in the southern district of the coastal town of Larnaca.
"We have collected evidence on a number of suspects and an area where these dog fights take place, which end when one dog dies," police spokesman Glafcos Xenos told Reuters.

Gruesome scenes of a fight involving a pit bull terrier and an alsatian dripping in blood and tearing at one another were shown on the Antenna private television station on Wednesday night, prompting a storm of protest calls to the government veterinary department on Thursday morning.
A group of people who had placed bets on the fight surrounded the animals in a field, pushing them towards one another with sticks.
"I must have got more than 200 phone calls from people horrified by what they saw. We are horrified," deputy director of the veterinary department George Efstathiou told Reuters.
"We won't let a bunch of criminals get away with this."
Cruelty to animals is punishable by up to six months in jail for first-time offenders or a 500 pound ($980) fine. The penalities are doubled for repeat offenders.

The veterinary department has started inspections of all dog breeding centres. Imports of pit bull terriers and three other breeds are banned under new legislation, but some pit bulls were imported to Cyprus before the new law took effect, Efstathiou said.
Last year animal rights groups expressed concern at indications they had of dog fights taking place, but at the time police said they had insufficient evidence to merit prosecution.
